newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end mostly lower. [CORRECTED 00:35 GMT 27/11]
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end mostly lower. [CORRECTED 00:35 GMT 27/11]

text.p: The Dow Industrial Average ended about 19 points lower after clawing its way back from steep losses caused by program trading.
Computer program trades sent the index higher shortly after the open, but then knocked a full 70 points off the average, triggering New York Stock Exchange curbs as the Dow fell 50 points.
The NYSE lifted the curbs on program trading only six minutes after they went into effect.
The Dow finished at 6529 unofficially on volume of 631 million on the New York Stock Exchange.
"You've got to expect a little bit more of a roller coaster and a dicier tape with the market this extended," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities.

Nie said despite today's setback, the recent strong bull trends still seem to be in place. He pointed to the Nasdaq Composite, which reversed earlier losses and posted a marginal gain to lift it to a new high.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.83 to 1281.2 unofficially.

Gary Anderson of Anderson & Loe Inc, which advises money managers, attributed the Dow's loss to profit-taking. "The market zigs and zags some, but but we are in a powerful up trend. This bull market has gored a lot of pundits who thought it was dead and went bearish. It ain't dead yet," he said.

Walt Disney Co shares surged 2-3/4 to 76-1/4 after it posted robust fourth quarter earnings reflecting record attendance at its theme parks and strong box office returns. Disney chairman Michael Eisner also said the earnings showed it was successfully integrating its recent purchase of ABC.

Declining stocks beat gaining stocks on the NYSE on heavy volume. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index fell one to about 766. The Russell 2000 Index, which measures smaller stocks, fell almost a point to 351.

The Dow was pulled lower by weakness in Caterpillar Inc, which sank 2-1/4 to 77-7/8 after industry rival Deere & Co reported net earnings per share that were below expectations for its fourth quarter (Corrects from "...Deere & Co reported slightly lower net earnings for its fourth quarter"). Deere fell 2-3/8 to 44.
Texaco shares also weighed on the index after news that groups would continue to boycott its products as part of a civil rights suit.
International Business Machines Corp closed up 1/8 to 158 but lost most of its earlier gains after Big Blue said it would buy up to $3.5 billion more of its common stock.
On the Nasdaq, Intel rose 2-1/4 to 123-3/4. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's semiconductor stock index rose 1.61 to 233.53.
Linens 'n Things Inc closed up 1/8 to 15-5/8 on volume of almost six million shares after its IPO. Another IPO, West TeleServices Corp rose 3-7/8 to 21-7/8.

The Dow Industrial Average fell 19.38 to 6528.41. Nasdaq Composite added 0.83 to 1281.20. NYSE Composite fell 0.88 to 397.98 on volume of 527,372,600. S&P's 500 Index fell 1.07 to 755.96. The American Stock Exchange index closed at 588.33, off 1.05. Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT.
